confidence_notes: Three web searches were run: one for the RBA rate and two for Gothenburg prices. The price searches returned aggregator and cost-of-living pages, including Numbeo-derived figures, in SEK. I converted them to USD at roughly 0.10 USD per SEK, which is my own approximation. Beer (about SEK 63-90 per 0.5 L), cappuccino (about SEK 40-50), the inexpensive meal (about SEK 120-150) and the mid-range dinner for two (about SEK 600-1,200) are reasonably supported. Wine and cocktail prices came from published ranges (wine about SEK 60-100 a glass, cocktail about SEK 100-170), with the chosen values set against the local beer price. All four accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Swedish and Gothenburg pricing. I did not search for accommodation prices or inspect any listings. They are the least certain anchors, particularly because July pricing varies with events and demand.
comparable_city_reasoning: Gothenburg is comparable to Stockholm, slightly cheaper for food and drink and accommodation, and to other high-cost Nordic cities such as Oslo and Copenhagen, which are more expensive.
